neighbours.label: 'first' introducing a historical first in a history narrative ('The first X was built in …')
fire: Paper money spread slowly through the region. Merchants distrusted it for decades. The first printed banknote appeared in 1661.
Rail travel changed the town forever. Before that, goods came by canal. The first passenger train arrived in 1840.
Ice was once cut from lakes and stored in sheds. The first electric refrigerator was sold to households in 1913.
Women campaigned for the vote for many years. The first country to grant it nationally was New Zealand.
Tea reached Europe through Dutch traders. The first tea shop in London opened its doors in 1717.
Early cars were noisy and unreliable. Roads were poor. The first speed limit was set at two miles per hour.
Monks kept bees in straw hives for centuries. The first movable-frame hive was patented in 1852.
Swimming became a sport in the nineteenth century. The first national championships were held in 1869.
quiet: Paper money spread slowly through the region. Merchants distrusted it for decades. Printed banknotes became common later on.
Rail travel changed the town forever. Before that, goods came by canal. Passenger trains arrived later in the century.
Ice was once cut from lakes and stored in sheds. Electric refrigerators were sold to households much later.
Women campaigned for the vote for many years. New Zealand granted it nationally in the end.
Tea reached Europe through Dutch traders. Tea shops in London grew popular with merchants.
Early cars were noisy and unreliable. Roads were poor. Speed limits were very low back then.
Monks kept bees in straw hives for centuries. Movable-frame hives were patented much later.
Swimming became a sport in the nineteenth century. National championships were soon held every year.
